punchline: The biggest muscle in your backside hardly works when you walk and works hard when you jog.
thirty_sec: In 2004 Dennis Bramble of Utah and Daniel Lieberman of Harvard argued in Nature that the human body was shaped by endurance running, which early humans may have taken up around 2 million years ago. Springy Achilles tendons, sweating and the gluteus maximus fit the idea. Fred Spoor of University College London said it was too early to know how the theory would be received.
